findings.endpoint: fasting glucose and lipids versus HbA1c in type 2 diabetes
findings.population: adults with type 2 diabetes (10 RCTs, 543 patients)
findings.finding_summary: This updated meta-analysis (10 RCTs, 543 patients; doses 120 mg to 6 g/day for 4-18 weeks) found cinnamon reduced fasting plasma glucose (-24.6 mg/dL), total cholesterol, LDL, and triglycerides and raised HDL — but had no significant effect on HbA1c (-0.16%, 95% CI -0.39 to 0.02).
findings.limitations: high heterogeneity across analyses (I-squared 66.5% to 94.7%); the fasting-glucose benefit without an HbA1c effect tempers the clinical meaning

findings.endpoint: metabolic measures in polycystic ovary syndrome
findings.finding_summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis informing the 2023 international PCOS guidelines (30 trials, n=2,230) found evidence of benefit for myo-inositol or D-chiro-inositol on some metabolic measures, no effect on other outcomes, and fewer gastrointestinal adverse events with myo-inositol than metformin.
findings.limitations: the guideline authors judge the overall evidence limited and inconclusive

findings.population: women with PCOS (subset of the same 30-trial review)
findings.finding_summary: The same guideline review found potential benefits from D-chiro-inositol for ovulation, within an evidence base it grades as limited and inconclusive.
findings.limitations: signal-level evidence only; the guideline stops short of a recommendation

findings.endpoint: HbA1c and fasting glucose in diabetes (by chromium formulation)
findings.population: adults with diabetes (14 RCTs, 875 participants; chloride, picolinate, brewer's yeast, and chromium-yeast forms)
findings.finding_summary: This meta-analysis (14 RCTs, 875 participants) analyzed each chromium formulation separately and found no statistically significant HbA1c effect for chromium yeast, brewer's yeast, or chromium picolinate, with at most a marginal fasting-glucose benefit from brewer's yeast.
findings.limitations: formulation-stratified analysis is the strength here — the null holds across the commonly sold forms

findings.endpoint: muscle mass preservation in older adults
findings.finding_summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis (7 RCTs) found greater muscle mass gain with HMB supplementation versus control (standardized mean difference 0.352, 95% CI 0.11 to 0.594, p=0.004), with no significant change in fat mass, concluding HMB can prevent lean-mass loss in older adults.
findings.limitations: small pooled population (287 total); strength and physical-function effects vary across later meta-analyses

findings.endpoint: body composition (fat-free mass and fat mass)
findings.population: adults in 18 randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trials
findings.finding_summary: This meta-analysis of 18 trials found fat-free mass increased during CLA treatment by a borderline 0.3 kg (p=0.05) with no dose or duration effect, and the same authors' prior meta-analysis found only modest fat loss — humans respond far less than the animal data suggested.
findings.limitations: effects are small enough to be of questionable practical relevance

findings.endpoint: symptomatic diabetic peripheral neuropathy (IV versus oral)
findings.population: patients with diabetic peripheral neuropathy (randomized controlled trials)
findings.finding_summary: This meta-analysis found intravenous alpha-lipoic acid 600 mg/day for 3 weeks produced a significant, clinically relevant reduction in neuropathic symptoms (SMD -2.8, 95% CI -4.2 to -1.5), while oral dosing above 600 mg/day for 3-5 weeks improved symptoms statistically (SMD -1.8) without meeting the threshold for clinical significance.
findings.limitations: the clinically-relevant result is intravenous — the oral supplement form most users take carries the weaker, clinically uncertain result
